title.narrative: IMPLEMENTING GCWA CONSERVATION PLAN IN CHIAPAS II

description.narrative: Partners will reduce Golden-cheeked Warbler (GCWA) habitat pressure due to deficient forest management practices in the State of Chiapas, the northernmost winter area for the species by working with forestry authorities such as SEMARNAT, CONAFOR and SEMAHN to develop tools that dictate the guidelines to follow for the evaluation and authorization of forest management programs using conservation criteria. Authorities are expected to adopt the instruments and together will initiate implementation in at least 4 forestry communities located within two Biosphere Reserves in Chiapas, La Sepultura and La Frailescana. Partners will have an indirect positive impact on 70,270 hectares of forests under state management and direct impact on 5,000 ha by implementing PMF with conservation criteria, will continue research and monitoring of GCWA in their winter range (Chiapas, Guatemala and Honduras), through flock monitoring to estimate abundance along the winter range; and a habitat characterization study in order to document winter requirement for the species. Additionally, partners will work to engage stakeholders from Latin American in the development of the Sierra Madre Pine-Oak and Cloud Forests / Western Coniferous Forests: Conservation Business Plan. This CBP includes a specific project focus on GCWA and the Central American Pine-Oak Forests. We will work together with Alliance partners and partners from US and Canada in developing this project, using Miradi and defining Strategies, Goals, Actions and Working Plans to be incorporated in this CBP.
